object_description: a large house framed by two low wings around a central garden
design_condition: The U-shaped complex occupies three plot edges, leaving a central garden connected to the castle park, while its low wings and placement along the historic boundaries respond to the slope, village, orchard, and castle.

positive.statement: The concept of the large house is plausible as a village-related volume and a sign of welcome.

position.rationale: The large house is clearly legible as the dominant U-shaped complex.

positive.statement: The dining room and the sequence from covered indoor terrace to outdoor terrace are high-quality spaces.

position.rationale: A southern central threshold zone approximates the interior-to-outdoor terrace sequence.

positive.statement: Placing the entire accommodation program on one level is a positive aspect of the proposal.

position.rationale: A low wing surface anchors the predominantly single-level accommodation.

positive.statement: The rooms’ relationship to the garden and landscape is well established, with privacy managed through successive thresholds.

position.rationale: The central garden and enclosing wings visibly establish successive spatial thresholds.

positive.statement: The historical issue is placed at the heart of the project, restoring the legibility of the monument and landscape.

position.rationale: The central garden is the identifiable project heart associated with landscape and monument legibility.

positive.statement: The modest elevation and flat green roof of the southeast wing contribute to good integration into the countryside.

position.rationale: The low southeast perimeter wing is localized on the eastern and southern edges.

positive.statement: The eastern walk connects existing and new paths and highlights western landscape views through belvedere squares.

position.rationale: The eastern perimeter provides the constrained location for paths and viewing spaces.

positive.statement: The protected central garden is welcoming and invites residents to wander.

position.rationale: The enclosed central void is clearly visible within the U-shaped footprint.

negative.statement: The entirely vertical distribution of common functions over four levels poses a usage problem for residents.

position.rationale: The full building envelope anchors the critique of vertically distributed common functions.

negative.statement: The limited clearance on the street is unsatisfactory as an EMS forecourt and village interface.

position.rationale: The southern street-facing edge is the plausible village and emergency-access interface.

negative.statement: The one-level accommodation bias creates a large built footprint on the site.

position.rationale: The extensive U-shaped footprint is directly visible in the plan and elevations.

negative.statement: The transformation toward military fort architecture with palisades is surprising and historically erroneous.

position.rationale: The western perimeter facade is used as an uncertain anchor for the expression critique.

negative.statement: The historic park is reduced because the orchard and vegetable garden largely disappear.

position.rationale: The northern and eastern exterior landscape is the plausible affected park edge.

negative.statement: The central garden establishes few relationships with the existing wooded park.

position.target: central garden relationship with wooded park
position.rationale: The central garden is visible, while its connection to the wooded park remains approximate.

negative.statement: The western facade remains essentially uninhabited despite the proposed fruit-tree alignment.

position.rationale: The western outer edge directly constrains the criticized facade location.
